questions.prompt: Which maps joint acceleration to inertial torque?
questions.explanation: The mass matrix is the inertia term in the dynamics equation.

questions.prompt: A point-mass pendulum (mass m = 1 kg on a massless rod of length l = 1 m, q measured from straight down) hangs at q = 0 rad and is at rest (q̇ = 0), with no damping. A torque τ = 2 N·m is applied at the pivot. Using m·l²·q̈ = τ − m·g·l·sin q, what is q̈ in rad/s²?
questions.explanation: At q = 0, sin q = 0, so gravity torque is zero. Then m·l²·q̈ = τ, i.e. q̈ = τ / (m·l²) = 2 / (1·1²) = 2 rad/s².

questions.prompt: A point mass m = 1 kg sits at distance l = 2 m from a pivot. Its joint inertia is I = m·l². What is I in kg·m²?
A frictionless pendulum has energy E = K + V. The power balance is dE/dt = q̇·(τ − b·q̇), where τ is the applied torque and b the damping coefficient. With τ = 0 and b = 0, what is dE/dt in watts?
questions.explanation: With τ = 0 and b = 0, dE/dt = q̇·(0 − 0) = 0 W: energy is conserved. Any measured gain in a simulation is a numerical or modelling error.

questions.prompt: A simulated pendulum gains energy with no input. Design tests to distinguish a gravity sign error from integration instability and parameter-unit mistakes.
rubric: State the model, units, and assumptions.
Show the reasoning and an independently checkable result.
Name a failure case and a verification experiment.
